chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man has missed prayers (qada) from the month of Ramadan, and he wakes up in the morning and does not eat until the afternoon prayer. Is it permissible for him to make that (fast) as a make-up fast from the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: Make-up (of missed obligatory acts, specifically prayers or fasting)

ai.seo_question: Can a person make up missed Ramadan prayers by fasting during the day without eating breakfast?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in making up missed Ramadan fasts (qada), specifically addressing the scenario where one delays suhoor (pre-dawn meal) until after dawn. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that the fast remains valid even if the person does not eat until the afternoon, highlighting the Shia juristic view that the essence of fasting is the abstention from food and drink during daylight hours, regardless of the timing of the last meal. This ruling underscores the practical ease (rukhas) granted to believers in fulfilling their religious obligations.
